clauses.current_legal_basis: The original text of EO 11302 (31 FR 11741) states no end for this clause, and no held later order, statute text or search result revokes or supersedes it (amendments are recorded as later events, not ends). The three selected machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, and the Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) record no revocation or supersession of EO 11302. The clause therefore continues on the original text, checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: The clause is the whole order. Section 1 allows the Administrator of Veterans Affairs to authorize actual necessary travel expenses including lodging and subsistence for claimants and beneficiaries; section 2 allows a mileage allowance and ferry, bridge, road and tunnel tolls in lieu of actual expenses; section 3 extends travel expenses to a non-employee attendant; section 4 permits payment before completion of travel for listed items; section 5 authorizes implementing rules; section 6 supersedes EO 11142 of February 12, 1964 (a one-time supersession performed on September 6, 1966, whose consequence persists). EO 11429 (September 9, 1968, 33 FR 12817) changed five cents a mile to six cents a mile in the first sentence of section 2; EO 11609 section 7(b) (July 22, 1971, 36 FR 13747) replaced the words allowance of not more than six cents a mile with an allowance in such amount per mile as the Administrator shall from time to time fix pursuant to 38 U.S.C. 111 as affected by that order. Those amendments changed the mileage rule in section 2 but the clause continues, amended. Current 38 CFR part 70 lists E.O. 11302 in its authority citations and nothing held ends the clause.

research_rationale:
EO 11302 (signed September 6, 1966; 31 FR 11741, Federal Register issue of September 8, 1966) prescribes regulations under 38 U.S.C. 111 governing travel expenses of claimants and beneficiaries of the Veterans' Administration. I read the complete held Federal Register text: authority paragraph and sections 1 to 6 (actual necessary travel expenses; a mileage allowance and tolls; attendants; payment before completion of travel; rule-making authority; supersession of EO 11142). The dossier inventory is one clause covering the whole order and I confirmed it without correction. The order has no end date or ending condition. Section 6 supersedes EO 11142 of February 12, 1964; that one-time supersession was performed when the order took effect and its consequence persists, so it is part of this single clause rather than an end of the order. EO 11429 (signed September 9, 1968; 33 FR 12817) amended the first sentence of section 2 to read six cents a mile in place of five cents, and EO 11609 (signed July 22, 1971; 36 FR 13747), section 7(b), further amended section 2 so that the allowance is in such amount per mile as the Administrator shall from time to time fix pursuant to 38 U.S.C. 111; EO 11609 section 12 makes it effective immediately except for certain paragraphs of its section 1. Both are later events on a continuing clause, not ends. The held current-law texts do not end the order: the eCFR (as of 2026-10-14) lists E.O. 11302 in the authority citations of 38 CFR part 70 (sections 70.1 to 70.4, 70.10, 70.20 and 70.21, 70.30 to 70.32, 70.40 to 70.42 and 70.50), the U.S. Code prints the order as a note to 38 U.S.C. 111 with no ending statement, and the catalog search records only the two amendments. The clause is operative as amended, checked through 2026-10-14.

savings.reason: EO 11302 has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause, and no held later order revokes or replaces it, so no residual effect arises. The travel-expense authorities in sections 1 to 5 are continuing authorizations, not accrued rights.
